english: Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix with real entries such that $\mathrm{tr}\left(A^{2}\right)=50$ and $\mathrm{tr}\left(AA^{T}\right)=250$, where $\mathrm{tr}(X)$ denotes the trace of a square matrix $X$ and $A^{T}$ is the transpose of $A$. Then the sum of the squares of all the entries of $A-A^{T}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A$ वास्तविक प्रविष्टियों वाला एक $3\times3$ आव्यूह है जिसके लिए $\mathrm{tr}\left(A^{2}\right)=50$ तथा $\mathrm{tr}\left(AA^{T}\right)=250$ है, जहाँ $\mathrm{tr}(X)$ वर्ग आव्यूह $X$ का अनुरेख है तथा $A^{T}$, $A$ का परिवर्त है। तब $A-A^{T}$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों के वर्गों का योग ______ है।
solution: So $\mathrm{tr}(K^{2})=-100$; sum of squares of entries of $A-A^{T}=2K$ is $\mathrm{tr}\left((2K)(2K)^{T}\right)=-4\,\mathrm{tr}(K^{2})=400$
solution_full: Every square matrix splits as $A=S+K$, where $S=\dfrac12\left(A+A^{T}\right)$ is symmetric and $K=\dfrac12\left(A-A^{T}\right)$ is skew-symmetric; then $A^{T}=S-K$ and $A-A^{T}=2K$.
For any square $X$, the sum of the squares of its entries is $\mathrm{tr}\left(XX^{T}\right)$. For $X=2K$: $\mathrm{tr}\left(2K\cdot2K^{T}\right)=-4\,\mathrm{tr}\left(K^{2}\right)$ since $K^{T}=-K$.
Therefore the sum of the squares of the entries of $A-A^{T}$ is $-4(-100)=400$.
originality_note: New: the two traces tr(A^2) and tr(AA^T) separate the symmetric and skew parts of an unknown matrix, giving the size of A - A^T without knowing A (way 4, a hidden invariant). Closest known: 'every square matrix is the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix' and 'tr(AA^T) = sum of squares of entries'. Different because: the combination of the two traces, with tr(SK) = 0, is the whole problem.
blueprint_concepts: Trace Properties: Tr(AB) = Tr(BA), trace of symmetric/skew-symmetric matrices.

concept_use.Trace Properties: Tr(AB) = Tr(BA), trace: tr(SK) = 0 for symmetric S and skew K (from tr(X^T) = tr(X) and tr(XY) = tr(YX)) removes the cross terms in tr(A^2) and tr(AA^T).
concept_use.Symmetric and skew symmetric Matrices: A = S + K with A^T = S - K, and A - A^T = 2K whose squared entries sum to -4 tr(K^2).

key_step: Splitting A = S + K and using tr(SK) = 0, so tr(A^2) and tr(AA^T) give tr(S^2) +- tr(K^2).
